content.title: About
content.content: Atole de chocolate is a traditional Mexican hot beverage made from corn masa, milk, sugar and cocoa. The drink has a thick, creamy texture and a rich chocolate flavor, often spiced with cinnamon or vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Atole dates back to pre‑Columbian Mexico, where it was prepared with maize and cacao.
It is traditionally served in clay mugs (cazuelas) to retain heat.
There are many regional variations: some add nuts, others use aromatics like anise or clove.
Atole is commonly served during holidays, especially Day of the Dead and Christmas.
The corn masa used in atole provides complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Corn masa and sugar give a quick boost of energy, useful in cold weather.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Corn fiber promotes healthy digestion and gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains calcium and magnesium
items.content: Milk and corn masa supply calcium and magnesium, important for bones and muscles.

items.title: Warm‑soothing effect
items.content: A hot drink helps warm the body and can have a calming effect on the nervous system.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels may be problematic for people with diabetes or weight concerns.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should use plant‑based milks.

items.title: Corn cross‑contamination
items.content: While corn is gluten‑free, some masa mixes can be contaminated with gluten, which matters for celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The thick beverage is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Atole de chocolate hot, typically in 200–250 ml cups. Add a pinch of cinnamon, vanilla, or a piece of chocolate for extra flavor. A dairy‑free version can be made with almond, oat, or other plant milks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry ingredients (masa, cocoa, sugar) in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Prepared atole is best consumed within 2–3 hours; leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated, though the texture may change.
